Olympia Stadium
Olympia Stadion | nickname = ''The First Stadium'' | image = OlympicRaceTrackOlympia.JPG | caption = | location = [[Olympia, Greece]] | coordinates = | broke_ground = | opened = 776 BC | closed = 393 AD | demolished = | owner = [[Ministry of Culture and Sports (Greece)|Ministry of Culture and Sports]] | operator = | surface = Grass, stones, dirt | Constructor = | construction_cost = | architect = | former_names = | tenants = | seating_capacity = 45,000 | dimensions = }} The '''Stadium at Olympia''' (also called the '''Olympia Stadium''' or the '''Olympia Stadion''') is an ancient stadium at the archaeological site of [[Olympia, Greece]], located to the east of the [[Temple of Zeus, Olympia|sanctuary of Zeus]]. It was the location of many of the sporting events at the [[Ancient Olympic Games]]. ==History== During the [[2004 Summer Olympics]], it hosted the [[Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics|shot put events]].{{cite news| url=https://www.arabnews.com/sports/news/913701| title=Flame for Rio Olympics is lit at birthplace of ancient Games| agency=[[Associated Press]]| date=21 April 2016| newspaper=[[Arab News]]| location=Riyadh| quote=...the ceremony continued in the ancient stadium — which was used at the 2004 Athens Games as the shot put venue.}}{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2004/aug/19/athensolympics2004.athletics2| title=Ancient and modern Shot put revisits Olympia| date=19 August 2004| access-date=12 March 2020| work=[[The Guardian]]| location=London}} == Features == The physical landmarks of the stadium are {{cvt|212.54|m}} long and {{cvt|30–34|m}} wide, and it served mainly for running races that determined the fastest person in the world. The track was made of hard-packed clay to serve as traction for the contestants in the running events.{{cite web| url=http://www.olympia-greece.org/stadium1.html| title=Ancient Stadium| website=www.olympia-greece.org| access-date=4 December 2017}} As in current day athletics, a white block was placed on one end of the track where the athletes would line up to place their feet and got ready to start of the race.{{cite news| url=https://www.worldhistory.org/image/428/| title=Starting Blocks, Olympia| work=[[World History Encyclopedia]]| first=Mark| last=Cartwright| date=24 April 2012| access-date=15 March 2020}} The white block was used to align all the athletes so they would all run the same distance. ==Gallery== File:Stadium at Olympia 2013.JPG|Stadium at Olympia Image:Toegang stadion.JPG|The vaulted tunnel leading into the stadium File:Start-finish line.jpg|Starting blocks inside the stadium Image:Judges' stand in side the Olympic Stadium.jpg|The judges' stand located on the south bank of the stadium ==See also== * [[Stadium of Delphi]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category-inline|Stadium of Olympia}} {{2004 Summer Olympic venues}} {{Olympic venues athletics}} {{coord|37|38|21|N|21|37|59|E|display=t|type:landmark}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Stadium at Olympia}} [[Category:Ancient Greek buildings and structures]] [[Category:Ancient Olympia]] [[Category:Olympic athletics venues]] [[Category:Sports venues in Greece]] [[Category:Stadiums]] [[Category:Venues of the 2004 Summer Olympics]]
